outcome: The conjecture (Borel's conjecture that every irrational algebraic number is normal, or at least normal in some base) remains completely open: no irrational algebraic number has been proven normal in any base since 26 January 2024. The one notable development is a December 2024 preprint (Kanado & Saito) that proves an equivalence between normality of a given algebraic irrational and the vanishing of a family of Riemann zeta function averages on vertical arithmetic progressions — a reformulation of the exact conjecture, not a resolution or a settled case of it, since the zeta-vanishing condition is itself unverified for any algebraic irrational.
summary: I traced this from the triage's found item, arXiv:2412.02337 (Kanado & Saito, 'Normality of algebraic numbers and the Riemann zeta function,' submitted 2024-12-03, revised 2024-12-17). I fetched the abstract and full text description directly: the authors prove that a positive algebraic irrational α is normal to base b if and only if a specific limit of Riemann zeta function averages over vertical arithmetic progressions vanishes for every integer k ≥ 0. This is a genuine mathematical result — an equivalence theorem — but it reformulates the exact conjecture in the bullet rather than settling any part of it: the zeta-vanishing side of the equivalence is exactly as unverified as the original normality question, so no case of the conjecture is removed and no bound moves. Per §3.1, this is scope-preserving (it's the same problem restated, not a restriction or a variant), but since neither side of the equivalence is established, it doesn't count as `partial` progress on the specific bullet — nothing has actually been settled. No journal publication or expert digestion (e.g., no Tao blog post, no Quanta coverage) of this paper turned up, and it has apparently not led to any follow-up proving the zeta condition for any specific algebraic number. Separately, I found a Google DeepMind 'formal-conjectures' GitHub repository (issue #2256, created 2025) that catalogues a Lean formalization of the *statement* of this conjecture as a benchmark target for automated theorem provers — this is explicitly not a proof attempt, just a formalized statement awaiting proof, and the repo's own text repeats that 'despite significant work, it is unknown whether even a single algebraic irrational number is normal in any base.' I also checked a 2017 paper on binary digits of algebraic irrationals (density bounds like √N growth in digit counts) but confirmed via its arXiv listing this predates the window and in any case only bounds digit density, which per §3.1's rule on existence/record questions doesn't move a normality question. The 2508.09319 paper on 'transcendentally normal numbers' is about transcendental numbers, a different class, and does not bear on algebraic irrationals. The current Wikipedia 'Normal number' article, fetched directly, confirms the conjecture is unresolved and cites no result past 2012 in its normality-of-algebraics section. No AI system appears anywhere in this chain: the zeta-equivalence paper is conventional human analytic number theory with no AI acknowledgement found, and the DeepMind repository's role is cataloguing/formalizing an unproved statement, not producing any part of a proof — so even that has no bearing on ai_role.
competing_reading: One could argue the Kanado-Saito equivalence deserves `progress` rather than `open`, on the theory that a clean equivalence to a well-studied analytic object (zeta function averages) is analogous to a bound moving — it changes the terrain future work would attack. But per the instructions a case must be *settled* (something removed from the open territory) to count as `partial`, and a bound must actually move numerically to count as `progress`; an equivalence where neither side is resolved settles nothing and moves no bound, so I classified it as `open` with `no_change_found` true. If a future update to this record found a paper verifying the zeta condition for a specific number (even conditionally), that would flip this to `claimed` or `partial`.
what_would_settle_it: A paper verifying the Kanado-Saito zeta-vanishing condition for any specific algebraic irrational (which would prove that number normal in that base), or a direct proof/counterexample for any algebraic irrational, or expert digestion of 2412.02337 in a survey or blog confirming its correctness and importance.
